Class Record

java.lang.Object
msfx.lib.md.Record
public class Record extends Object
A list of values with their column definitions.

Records are meant to exist in large numbers, as in a record set, so all the records of a set share the same ColumnList, and each record only adds its array of values. For the same reason the constructor does not check that the values match the column types: check it once, with validate(ColumnList, Value[]), before reading a large number of records.

The array of values is used as is, not copied.

Author:
Miquel Sas

  • Method Details

    • validate

      public static void validate(ColumnList columns, Value[] values)
      Checks that the values match the columns: same number, no null references, and each value of the same type as its column. Meant to be called once before creating a large number of records with the same columns.
      Parameters:
      columns - The columns.
      values - The values.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If the columns or the values are null, their sizes differ, a value is null or its type is not the type of its column.

    • checkSizes

      public static void checkSizes(ColumnList columns, Value[] values)
      Checks that neither the columns nor the values are null and that there is one value per column. This is the check the constructor does on every record; it does not check the value types, see validate(ColumnList, Value[]).
      Parameters:
      columns - The columns.
      values - The values.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If the columns or the values are null, or their sizes differ.

      public Value getValue(String alias)
